input: Convert /data/employees.json (an array of objects with keys name, department, salary) to CSV format with a header row. Save the result to /data/employees.csv and print it. The output should have the header 'name,department,salary' followed by one data row per object.

transcript.final_response:
Converted `/data/employees.json` to CSV format and saved to `/data/employees.csv`.

```csv
name,department,salary
Alice Chen,Engineering,120000
Bob Park,Marketing,95000
Carol Wu,Engineering,115000
Dave Kim,Sales,88000
```
tool_calls:
ls -la /data
head -n 20 /data/employees.json
which jq node awk sed
jq -r '["name","department","salary"], (.[] | [.name, .department, .salary]) | @csv' /data/employees.json
cat /data/employees.json
jq -r '["name", "department", "salary"], (.[] | [.name, .department, (.salary | tostring)]) | join(",")' /data/employees.json
jq -r '["name", "department", "salary"], (.[] | [.name, .department, (.salary | tostring)]) | join(",")' /data/employees.json > /data/employees.csv
cat /data/employees.csv
ls -la /data/employees.csv

tool_outputs.commands:

head -n 20 /data/employees.json
which jq node awk sed
